podcast.body: Summer's first American album, released jointly by Moroder's Oasis label and Casablanca Records in late summer 1975. Its 17-minute title track, a re-recorded and expanded version of the single, took up the entire Side A. The album was the first in its genre to feature a full-side suite and sold unusually well for a disco LP, going gold and peaking at number 11 on the Billboard album chart, alongside LPs by artists like Electric Light Orchestra and Peter Frampton. "Love to Love You Baby, Summer's First American Album Release, issued jointly by Moroder's Oasis label and Casablanca Records in the late summer of 1975."

This extended version was conceived after Neil Bogart, founder of Casablanca Records, observed the mood-setting power of the original shorter track at a party and sought to create a record specifically for relaxation and lovemaking without interruption. "Well, Neil Bogart got a 17-minute version, which became the entire side, side one of the album love to love you, baby."
